paragraphs: Contrastive learning builds representations by learning which samples belong together and which do not. This paper asks why representations learned from augmented, unlabeled data can support later prediction tasks. It develops a statistical framework centered on approximate sufficient statistics: representations that preserve information well enough to remain useful for subsequent inference.

The authors focus on SimCLR and extend a notion of approximate sufficiency previously formulated for image–text learning using KL-divergence. They establish equivalent formulations and broaden the framework to general f-divergences. Within this analysis, minimizing SimCLR and other contrastive objectives produces encoders with approximate sufficiency, connecting the training objective to an information-preservation property.

The paper then connects that property to downstream regression and classification. Performance depends both on how close the encoder is to sufficient and on errors introduced by data augmentation. Examples involving linear regression and topic classification illustrate the connection. The resulting account explains downstream usefulness through what the representation retains and how augmentation affects that retained information.
neurips-2025-a-statistical-theory-of-con.tldr: A statistical framework connects contrastive learning to approximate information preservation and explains how that supports downstream prediction.

paragraphs: Graph quantification asks what fraction of vertices belongs to each label category. Its target is the distribution across a collection of vertices, so the central question concerns aggregate composition. This paper extends Adjusted Classify & Count, or ACC, to this setting, broadening a problem previously approached through node clustering.

A central obstacle is that ACC relies on prior probability shift, an assumption about how label frequencies can change between settings. The authors show that this assumption often does not apply to graph quantification. They introduce structural importance sampling to address structural covariate shift, making changes in graph-related characteristics part of the quantification approach.

The paper also introduces Neighborhood-aware ACC to improve estimates when edges connect vertices with different labels. This addresses a separate structural issue: connected vertices need not belong to the same category. Evaluations across multiple graph quantification tasks support both techniques. Together, the contributions adapt aggregate label estimation to changes in graph structure and to neighborhoods whose labels are mixed.
neurips-2025-adjusted-count-quantificati.tldr: Two graph-aware methods improve label-distribution estimation under structural shifts and connections between differently labeled vertices.

paragraphs: Recognizing architectural symbols in CAD drawings requires interpreting detailed collections of drawing elements. This paper addresses both the supply of labeled training data and the model used to recognize those symbols. Its annotation engine uses attributes already present in systematically archived CAD drawings to generate annotations automatically, reducing the need for manual labeling.

The resulting ArchCAD-400K dataset contains 413,062 chunks drawn from 5,538 highly standardized drawings. The authors describe it as more than 26 times larger than the largest existing CAD dataset, with greater drawing diversity and broader symbol categories. Annotations reach down to individual lines, providing supervision at the level of the drawing elements from which symbols are formed.

The accompanying Dual-Pathway Symbol Spotter combines primitive features with complementary image features through an adaptive fusion module. This lets the model draw on both the constituent drawing elements and their visual appearance. Experiments report state-of-the-art performance and improved robustness, supporting the value of pairing a larger annotated resource with a model designed to combine these information sources.
neurips-2025-archcad-400k-a-large-scale-.tldr: ArchCAD-400K pairs automatically annotated architectural drawings with a symbol-recognition model that combines primitive and image features.

paragraphs: This paper investigates whether the linear transformations inside neural networks can be understood through a small collection of geometric building blocks. The motivation is compositionality: simple operations may combine to produce richer functions, but the underlying primitives remain poorly understood. Linear layers provide a concrete setting in which to study this idea algebraically.

Using Clifford algebra, the authors express linear layers through compositions of bivectors, geometric objects that encode oriented planes. They introduce a differentiable algorithm that decomposes these transformations into products of rotors. The proposed construction uses O(log² d) parameters, compared with O(d²) for a dense matrix, giving the geometric formulation a substantial parameter-efficiency advantage.

The authors apply rotor-based layers to the key, query, and value projections in language-model attention. In these evaluations, performance matches strong block-Hadamard and low-rank approximation baselines. The findings support geometric composition as a useful way to construct compact attention projections, while offering an algebraic perspective on how elementary transformations can combine into higher-level functions.
neurips-2025-composing-linear-layers-fro.tldr: Rotor-based linear layers use compact geometric compositions and match strong approximation baselines in language-model attention projections.

paragraphs: Low-rank adaptation fine-tunes a model through compact parameter updates. Existing approaches often adapt individual Transformer layers independently, but the authors find that directly carrying this approach over to convolutional networks gives unsatisfactory results. Their explanation centers on the strong correlations between successive convolutional layers, which make independent adaptations a poor fit.

CoLoRA explicitly models these inter-layer dependencies using correlated low-rank matrices. It also adds a filtering method that introduces no trainable parameters and expands the receptive field of the adaptation. The aim is to reduce interference from local regions that contribute little useful information, improving how efficiently the limited adaptation parameters are used.

Experiments cover image classification, semantic segmentation, and object detection, with reported improvements over state-of-the-art parameter-efficient approaches. In the specific combination of ConvNeXt-S and VTAB-1k image classification, CoLoRA exceeds full fine-tuning while using only 5% trainable parameters. This result shows that coordinating updates across layers can make a small adaptation budget particularly effective in that evaluated setting.
neurips-2025-correlated-low-rank-adaptat.tldr: CoLoRA makes parameter-efficient ConvNet tuning more effective by coordinating low-rank updates across correlated layers.

paragraphs: How many hidden layers does a ReLU network need to represent a continuous piecewise-linear function exactly? This paper advances that open question through the concrete task of computing the maximum of several numbers. Exact representation is central here: the results concern reproducing the function precisely, rather than obtaining a sufficiently close numerical approximation.

The main theorem applies to networks compatible with a particular geometric structure called the braid fan. Under that restriction, computing the maximum of d numbers requires at least Ω(log log d) hidden layers. The authors also give a combinatorial proof that computing the maximum of five numbers requires three hidden layers within this class, replacing an earlier computational verification.

A separate construction concerns maxout networks. A rank-3 maxout layer followed by a rank-2 layer suffices to compute the maximum of seven numbers, showing that a natural extension of an existing upper bound is not tight. Together, these results sharpen depth requirements and constructions, while the braid-fan assumption remains essential to the stated ReLU lower bounds.
neurips-2025-depth-bounds-for-neural-net.tldr: For braid-fan-compatible ReLU networks, the paper proves growing depth requirements for exact maximum computation and sharpens related maxout constructions.

paragraphs: First-person vision benchmarks usually emphasize what people do, handle, or attend to. egoEMOTION adds emotional state and personality to that picture, aiming to represent internal factors that can shape behavior. The dataset combines recordings from controlled emotion-elicitation tasks and natural activities with frequent participant reports about their own affect.

The resource contains more than 50 hours from 43 participants wearing Project Aria glasses. Sessions synchronize eye-tracking video, head-mounted photoplethysmography, motion measurements, and reference physiological baselines. Emotion reports use the Circumplex Model and Mikels’ Wheel, while personality is described through the Big Five framework. This combination connects observed behavior and physiological measurements with participants’ reported experiences.

The authors define tasks for classifying valence, arousal, and dominance, recognizing discrete emotions, and inferring personality traits. A simple classical learning baseline produces better real-world affect estimates from egocentric-system signals than from physiological signals in their comparison. The dataset therefore creates a concrete basis for studying emotion and personality alongside the physical activities already central to egocentric perception.
neurips-2025-egoemotion-egocentric-visio.tldr: egoEMOTION combines first-person recordings, physiological measurements, and self-reports to benchmark emotion recognition and personality inference.

paragraphs: Network traffic classifiers depend on training labels that can be wrong because of human mistakes or inaccurate automated labeling. These errors can make learned classifications unreliable. FlowRefiner addresses this problem through a framework that identifies questionable labels, refines them, and trains a classifier designed to remain robust when label noise is present.

Its first component uses traffic semantics extracted by a pretrained encoder to detect potentially mislabeled flows. A confidence-guided correction component then fine-tunes a label predictor to produce refined training flows. The final classifier learns at both the flow and packet levels, combining patterns from the overall communication sequence with patterns in its constituent packets.

The authors evaluate the framework on four traffic datasets, covering different classification scenarios and noise ratios. They report that it reduces the effects of label noise and consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines by a large margin. The contribution is a coordinated treatment of noisy supervision: semantic detection and label correction improve the training material, while learning across granularities strengthens the resulting classifier.
neurips-2025-flowrefiner-a-robust-traffi.tldr: FlowRefiner improves traffic classification with noisy labels by combining semantic noise detection, confidence-guided correction, and packet- and flow-level learning.

paragraphs: A connectome records neural wiring, but wiring alone omits properties such as synaptic strengths, neuronal thresholds, and time constants. This paper asks how much measured structure can constrain circuit function by studying the fruit fly’s head-direction circuit. That circuit maintains an internal heading estimate and updates it using self-motion velocity signals.

The authors combine self-supervised and unsupervised objectives to estimate missing parameters at the level of cell types. Starting from the raw connectivity matrix, their method recovers continuous attractor dynamics and accurate integration across a range of velocity inputs. It achieves this with minimal tuning even though the measured wiring lacks the symmetric regularity of an idealized ring attractor.

The study also examines how departures from the original connectome change the set of viable solutions. Simulated ablations probe the distinct contributions of particular cell types. The findings show how measured connectivity, supplemented by limited biologically grounded parameter adjustment, can reproduce known physiology and help explain circuit function without requiring independently tuned parameters for every neuron and synapse.
neurips-2025-from-synapses-to-dynamics-o.tldr: A model built from fruit-fly connectivity recovers head-direction dynamics using limited tuning of missing parameters at the cell-type level.

paragraphs: This paper studies how to estimate the edge-density parameter of an Erdős–Rényi graph when an adversary can alter every edge touching a selected fraction of its nodes. Such corruption can substantially distort the observed graph. The objective is to recover the underlying parameter accurately despite those arbitrary additions and removals.

The authors give a polynomial-time algorithm whose additive error matches information-theoretic lower bounds up to logarithmic factors in the corruption fraction. It works when the expected-degree parameter is at least constant order and reaches the optimal one-half breakdown threshold. The guarantee also covers sparse graphs, including a regime where previous methods had substantially suboptimal errors.

The algorithm uses the sum-of-squares hierarchy. Its key ingredient is a constant-degree certificate controlling how many edges touch small vertex sets in the underlying random graph. Establishing that such certificates exist even in the sparse regime enables the improved guarantees. The result combines computational efficiency, near-optimal statistical accuracy, and an optimal corruption threshold within the stated random-graph model.
neurips-2025-improved-robust-estimation-.tldr: A polynomial-time estimator achieves near-optimal error and the optimal breakdown threshold for node-corrupted Erdős–Rényi graphs, including sparse ones.

paragraphs: Vertical federated learning allows collaborators to train a model using different features held by different clients. Evaluating these methods realistically is difficult because privacy concerns limit the availability of public data from such collaborations. MARS-VFL addresses this evaluation gap with a benchmark built around data from practical applications involving distributed features.

The benchmark keeps those applications compatible with the vertical federated setting and standardizes evaluation along three dimensions: efficiency, robustness, and security. Bringing these dimensions into a shared framework gives researchers a common basis for comparing approaches. The authors conduct comprehensive experiments across different methods to provide reference results for that evaluation process.

The paper also unifies the evaluation of robustness challenges in vertical federated learning and introduces a method aimed at addressing them. This supplies baseline methods alongside the benchmark itself. The overall contribution is an evaluation resource and protocol: it connects practical collaboration settings with consistent assessments of computational behavior, resilience, and security, creating a clearer foundation for subsequent methodological comparisons.
neurips-2025-mars-vfl-a-unified-benchmar.tldr: MARS-VFL standardizes realistic evaluation of vertical federated learning across efficiency, robustness, and security.

paragraphs: A sparse additive model represents an outcome using a small set of separate functions, each associated with one input variable. This preserves interpretability while allowing flexible relationships. The paper studies how to identify which component functions are active, asking how strong their signals must be for reliable selection in a high-dimensional setting.

The authors establish minimax separation rates under two definitions of success. One controls false discoveries and false negatives across multiple selection decisions. The other controls the probability of recovering the wrong active set altogether. These perspectives distinguish managing the overall pattern of selection mistakes from correctly identifying every active component as a single joint decision.

The paper also studies the effect of unknown function smoothness and proposes an adaptive selection procedure. Its final finding separates two goals that can otherwise seem interchangeable: accurately estimating the additive function and identifying its active components. A procedure with optimal estimation performance may still fail to attain optimal selection performance, so good predictive reconstruction alone does not settle the variable-selection problem.
neurips-2025-minimax-optimal-univariate-.tldr: The paper establishes optimal signal requirements for selecting sparse additive components and shows that optimal estimation need not imply optimal selection.

paragraphs: Building a small model for a narrow task sounds straightforward, but the paper identifies obstacles in how neural networks acquire and organize skills. It examines both learning a specialized model from scratch and extracting a desired skill from a larger general model. These routes encounter different aspects of the network’s internal representation.

In synthetic-task experiments, learning certain narrow skills sometimes requires training on a broader data distribution. The effect appears when skills depend on one another hierarchically. Broad training supplies a curriculum that substantially accelerates learning, meaning that examples outside the final narrow target can contribute to acquiring the capabilities that target depends on.

For skill transfer, the authors find that capabilities are often not perfectly confined to components that can simply be retained or pruned. Even so, pruning-based approaches can outperform distillation in their study. They also investigate regularization that aligns desired skills with prunable components while unlearning unnecessary ones. The results identify both hierarchical learning dependencies and distributed skill storage as challenges for creating strong specialized models.
neurips-2025-on-the-creation-of-narrow-a.tldr: Synthetic experiments show how skill dependencies and distributed representations can complicate training or extracting narrowly specialized models.

paragraphs: Latent diffusion models can produce convincing local edits while leaving small inconsistencies where edited and original content meet. Compression into a latent representation can introduce color shifts, mismatched textures, and visible seams. PixPerfect addresses these pixel-level problems with a refinement framework intended to work across different latent diffusion architectures and editing tasks.

The framework uses a differentiable discriminative pixel space to make subtle color and texture discrepancies more apparent and support their suppression. A training pipeline simulates realistic editing artifacts so the refiner encounters the problems it will need to repair. Refinement then operates directly in pixel space, supporting applicability across different latent representations.

Experiments cover inpainting, object removal, and object insertion. The authors report substantial improvements in perceptual fidelity and downstream editing performance across these benchmarks. The approach matters because successful local editing requires both a plausible changed region and visual consistency with its surroundings. PixPerfect makes that consistency a direct training and refinement target, with reported benefits across several forms of localized image manipulation.
neurips-2025-pixperfect-seamless-latent-.tldr: PixPerfect refines edited images in pixel space to reduce seams, color shifts, and texture mismatches across latent diffusion editing tasks.

paragraphs: Synthetic-image detectors can be tested by generating images that they mistakenly accept as real. Existing approaches often require access to detector internals or expensive optimization for each image. PolyJuice instead uses black-box detector access to learn an image-independent steering direction, making the same learned intervention reusable across generated images.

The method starts from an observed difference in the text-to-image model’s latent-space distributions for correctly and incorrectly classified samples. A lightweight offline process estimates the direction of that shift. Generation is then steered toward detector failure modes. The authors also show that directions estimated at lower resolutions can transfer to higher resolutions through interpolation, reducing computational overhead.

The reported deception improvements reach up to 84% relative to unsteered generation. The authors additionally use PolyJuice-generated examples to augment detector training, reporting detector performance improvements of up to 30%. These findings connect reusable failure discovery with detector improvement: the same process that exposes weaknesses can provide training examples for strengthening the evaluated detection systems.
neurips-2025-polyjuice-makes-it-real-bla.tldr: PolyJuice learns reusable black-box steering directions that expose synthetic-image detector failures and supply examples for improving detectors.

paragraphs: PRSformer addresses disease-risk prediction from individual genetic records containing very large numbers of variants. The aim is to retain individual-level information while learning interactions that linear predictors may miss. It uses a multitask architecture, allowing one model to learn predictions for several diseases directly from genotype inputs.

Neighborhood attention keeps each layer’s computational complexity linear in the number of variants. Stacking these layers progressively expands the effective receptive field: the model first captures local dependencies, such as those within linkage disequilibrium blocks, and then integrates information across wider genomic regions. This design makes attention tractable while supporting potentially nonlinear and long-range interactions.

The study uses a private cohort of approximately five million people and 140,000 variants to predict 18 autoimmune and inflammatory conditions. PRSformer outperforms optimized linear models trained on the same individual data and LDPred2 derived from the same cohort. Its nonlinear advantage emerges mainly above one million samples, and multi-ancestry training improves generalization in the reported experiments, tying the gains to both scale and training-population composition.
neurips-2025-prsformer-disease-predictio.tldr: PRSformer uses scalable neighborhood attention for genetic disease prediction, with nonlinear benefits emerging primarily in million-plus-person training sets.

paragraphs: Urban data systems often separate predicting regional characteristics from retrieving geographic objects. UrbanSparse brings these tasks into a shared framework, seeking to reduce duplicated computation and let their representations support one another. Its central design combines sparse encodings suited to detailed queries with dense representations suited to capturing urban meaning.

Bloom filter-based encodings compress highly sparse geographic queries and fine-grained text terms for retrieval. A dense semantic codebook captures granular urban features for prediction. Two-view contrastive learning connects representations of urban objects, regions, and contexts. These components give the combined system ways to preserve query detail while also learning features useful across prediction tasks.

On real-world datasets, the authors report prediction-accuracy gains of 25.16% and retrieval-precision improvements of 20.76% over state-of-the-art baselines, alongside 65.97% faster training. The results support the proposed shared architecture in the evaluated settings. They suggest that geospatial prediction and retrieval can benefit from coordinated representation learning while reducing the burden associated with maintaining separately trained systems.
neurips-2025-reconciling-geospatial-pred.tldr: UrbanSparse combines sparse query encodings and dense urban representations to improve geospatial prediction, retrieval, and training speed.

paragraphs: A GUI agent must connect a user’s instruction to the precise interface element it should act on. This grounding step becomes difficult in dense, high-resolution professional interfaces. SE-GUI addresses it with reinforcement learning, motivated by the large data requirements and weak generalization the authors identify in traditional supervised fine-tuning approaches.

The framework combines three strategies. Carefully curated seed examples provide a high-quality starting point. A dense policy gradient supplies continuous feedback based on prediction accuracy. An iterative reinforcement fine-tuning process then uses attention maps to refine the model. Together, these strategies focus on the quality of training examples, the informativeness of feedback, and repeated model improvement.

With 3,000 training samples, the seven-billion-parameter model achieves state-of-the-art results among similarly sized models on three grounding benchmarks. It reaches 47.3% accuracy on ScreenSpot-Pro and outperforms substantially larger models, including UI-TARS-72B. These results support the effectiveness of the combined reinforcement-learning approach for interface grounding, particularly in the complex, high-resolution environments emphasized by the study.
neurips-2025-se-gui-enhancing-visual-gro.tldr: SE-GUI combines curated examples, dense accuracy feedback, and attention-guided refinement to improve interface grounding with 3,000 training samples.

paragraphs: Clinical diagnosis often unfolds through questions, examinations, and investigations that gradually reduce uncertainty. VivaBench evaluates this sequential process through interactive scenarios modeled on oral medical examinations. Its purpose is to assess how a language-model agent acquires and combines information, extending evaluation beyond questions that supply a complete clinical presentation at the outset.

The benchmark contains 1,762 physician-curated clinical vignettes. Agents must actively seek relevant findings, choose investigations, and synthesize evidence over multiple turns before arriving at a diagnosis. This setup makes the path through the case part of the assessment, exposing decisions about which information to request and when the available evidence supports a conclusion.

The evaluated models perform substantially worse in this iterative setting than when diagnosing well-described presentations. Reported failures include fixation on initial hypotheses, inappropriate investigation ordering, premature closure, and missed screening for critical conditions. These findings show why competence on complete clinical questions does not establish competence in sequential diagnostic reasoning. VivaBench provides a standardized way to examine that gap and the decision trajectories behind it.
neurips-2025-simulating-viva-voce-examin.tldr: VivaBench reveals substantial weaknesses when language models must gather evidence and reason through clinical cases over multiple turns.

paragraphs: Federated learning is often studied as though each client already has a fixed dataset. This paper examines clients that continuously collect data, with successive samples linked through Markov processes. Such dependence matters because observations arriving close together can carry overlapping information, changing the statistical behavior assumed in analyses based on independent sampling.

The authors analyze Minibatch SGD, Local SGD, and a momentum variant of Local SGD. Under standard assumptions and smooth, non-convex client objectives, they show that collaborative learning still provides a sample-complexity benefit proportional to the inverse of the number of clients. Communication complexity remains comparable to the independently sampled setting.

Temporal dependence nevertheless carries a cost: sample complexity remains higher for Markovian streams than for independent data. Experiments using real pollution-monitoring time series validate the analysis. The result therefore preserves a qualified case for federation with streaming observations: adding clients can improve statistical efficiency under the stated assumptions, even though collaboration does not eliminate the extra difficulty introduced by dependence over time.
neurips-2025-streaming-federated-learnin.tldr: Under stated assumptions, federated learning retains client-scaling benefits with Markovian streams, although temporal dependence increases sample requirements.

paragraphs: Hierarchical clustering organizes data into a tree that offers partitions at different levels of detail. This paper asks how much more can be obtained from an existing cluster tree. It shows that a suitable hierarchy can support efficient optimization of center-based clustering objectives, including k-means, over that hierarchy.

The theoretical result applies to any hierarchy satisfying the paper’s reasonableness condition. Beyond finding an optimal solution for an objective over the supplied hierarchy, the authors show that these solutions themselves form hierarchies. Consequently, a starting tree can give access to additional meaningful trees, each offering its own collection of partitions for exploratory analysis.

This changes the role of the original hierarchy from a single menu of clusterings into a basis for generating many alternatives. The authors report that these alternatives can be accessed very quickly and verify their utility across datasets, input hierarchies, and partitioning schemes. The optimality claim concerns objectives solved over the given hierarchy, making that structure the foundation for both the computational result and the resulting cluster organization.
neurips-2025-ultrametric-cluster-hierarc.tldr: A suitable cluster tree supports fast, optimal center-based clustering over its hierarchy, with solutions that form additional hierarchies.

paragraphs: Objects have physical properties that visual inspection alone cannot fully reveal. VTV-LLM connects visual and tactile video information with language so an embodied system can describe and reason about those properties. The paper addresses both the data needed for this integration and the training process for combining information across sensors and modalities.

Its VTV150K dataset contains 150,000 video frames from 100 objects recorded using GelSight Mini, DIGIT, and Tac3D tactile sensors. Annotations cover hardness, protrusion, elasticity, and friction. Training proceeds through three stages: strengthening visuo-tactile representations, aligning them with text, and fine-tuning with text prompts to support natural-language generation.

The resulting framework supports assessment of tactile features, comparisons between them, and decisions grounded in scenarios. Experimental evaluations report superior performance on tactile reasoning tasks. The contribution is a bridge from sensor observations to language-based physical understanding: it gives tactile measurements a role in reasoning about objects and interactions, alongside the visual information that existing multimodal approaches already emphasize.
neurips-2025-universal-visuo-tactile-vid.tldr: VTV-LLM combines visual and tactile video with language using a multisensor dataset and staged training for tactile reasoning.

paragraphs: Reconstructing tissue in three dimensions from serial electron-microscopy sections requires correcting misalignment and distortions introduced during sectioning. The difficult part is preserving genuine biological shape changes while removing preparation artifacts. This paper formulates registration as continuous trajectory optimization, treating consistency across sections and preservation of local structure as linked objectives.

The method uses a dual objective that balances global trajectory smoothness with local structural preservation. Its solver combines Gauss–Seidel iteration with Neural ODEs, integrating biophysical priors and data-driven deformation compensation. This gives the optimization an explicit way to encourage coherent reconstruction while retaining the detailed morphological variation that the reconstruction is meant to reveal.

Training is fully unsupervised and requires no ground-truth registrations, matching a setting where annotations are difficult to obtain. Experiments across multiple datasets and tissue types report superior structural restoration accuracy and cross-tissue robustness. The findings support continuous trajectory modeling as a way to manage the tension between correcting sectioning distortions and maintaining faithful biological organization throughout a reconstructed volume.
neurips-2025-unsupervised-trajectory-opt.tldr: An unsupervised Neural ODE registration framework balances smooth reconstruction with preservation of local tissue structure in serial electron microscopy.

paragraphs: Perturbation guidance steers image generation by constructing a weakened version of a model and guiding sampling away from its behavior. This paper studies where attention perturbations should be applied in Diffusion Transformers. Its analysis moves from whole layers to individual attention heads, identifying heads associated with visual structure, style, and texture quality.

HeadHunter iteratively selects attention heads according to user-centered objectives, allowing more targeted control over generation. SoftPAG then adjusts perturbation strength by interpolating each selected attention map toward an identity matrix. This creates a continuous control over how strongly a head is altered, helping suppress artifacts associated with the intervention.

The authors report that this approach reduces oversmoothing from layer-level perturbations and enables style manipulation through combinations of selected heads. Evaluations on Stable Diffusion 3 and FLUX.1 show superior general quality enhancement and style-specific guidance. The findings connect interpretable specialization within attention layers to practical generation controls, with both the choice of heads and the strength of perturbation contributing to the resulting image.
neurips-2025-where-and-how-to-perturb-on.tldr: HeadHunter and SoftPAG target individual attention heads and continuously tune perturbations to improve image quality and style control.

paragraphs: Blind-spot denoising learns to predict hidden image pixels from surrounding observations. Real-world noise complicates this approach when nearby pixels have strongly correlated noise. Attempts to weaken that correlation can also disrupt useful relationships among pixel values, creating a trade-off between removing shared noise and preserving the image structure needed for accurate prediction.

The paper analyzes this trade-off theoretically by considering replacements with weaker noise correlation but potentially lower similarity. It quantifies how both factors affect statistical estimation risk. Guided by that analysis, the proposed method refills masked locations using distant pixels with similar appearances and lower noise correlation, balancing the two properties in its computational scheme.

The authors report that this strategy outperforms existing zero-shot blind-spot denoising methods in experiments. Its significance lies in treating replacement-pixel selection as a balance between statistical and visual compatibility. A useful replacement should reduce the influence of correlated noise while retaining enough similarity to preserve the dependencies that help reconstruct the underlying image.
neurips-2025-zero-shot-blind-spot-image-.tldr: The method improves blind-spot denoising by refilling masked pixels with distant, similar observations that have less-correlated noise.
